extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners/agents) handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive MPEP rules governing ex parte reexamination practice: time extensions, panel review, after-final practice, appeals, appeal briefs, examiner answers, and Board review of SNQ issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c); requests must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply in reexamination proceedings (those provisions apply only to “an applicant”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for an extension in a third party requested ex parte reexamination must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due; mere filing of a request will not effect any extension. A third-party request for extension will be granted only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. For patent-owner requested ex parte reexaminations (including 35 U.S.C. 257), a request for up to two months from the time period set in the Office action must be filed no later than two months from the expiration of the time period set in the Office action. A request for more than two months must be filed on or before the day action is due and mere filing will not effect the extension. The time for taking action in a patent-owner requested ex parte reexamination will not be extended for more than two months from the time period set in the Office action in the absence of sufficient cause or for more than a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic two-month extension on timely first response to final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a timely first response to a final rejection is construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period for an additional two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An automatic extension applies even to an informal or unsigned timely first response. However, the statutory period for response will not expire later than SIX MONTHS from the mailing date of the final action. Advisory Office action PTOL-467 will inform the patent owner of the automatic two-month extension. No additional 'no cause' extensions are available beyond the PLT-conforming minimum without showing sufficient cause (see 37 CFR 1.550(c)(3) and MPEP § 2265).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and bracket insertions in reexamination correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs are designated for use only in reexamination proceedings and contain brackets where the examiner must insert dates/periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes: this form paragraph may be used only in reexamination proceedings; in bracket 1 insert filing date of amendment (or appropriate period for response), and in bracket 2 insert appropriate period for response (normally TWO (2) MONTHS). Also, as with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review: composition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review is conducted at each stage of the examiner's examination in an ex parte reexamination proceeding (except for notices of informality or incomplete response), to review the examiner's preliminary decision to reject and/or allow claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel make-up: three or more members including a manager, the examiner in charge, and a third member selected by the manager; conferees should be primary examiners knowledgeable in the technology or experienced in reexamination practice. The majority of conferees should not have been involved in the original examination. An 'original' examiner should only be chosen as a conferee if they are the most knowledgeable or there is a specific justifiable reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review: process and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel members confer and review patentability; if the conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision, the Office action is issued and signed by the examiner with other conferees initialing; if not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conferees initial the action even if dissenting. If the examiner in charge disagrees with the conference decision, the manager will generally assign the proceeding to another examiner. Panels review all issues of patentability and procedural matters affecting patentability to provide a comprehensive discussion and finding for each issue. Matters outside the examiner's jurisdiction (petitions, extensions of time, CRU support staff notices) are not panel-reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and challenge procedure for failure to hold panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a panel review is not held, the patent owner or third party requester who wishes to object must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of this fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The failure to hold a panel review will be noted by absence of conferees' initials. Any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action or it will not be considered. In no event will failure to hold a panel review, by itself, be grounds for vacating Office decisions or 'restarting' the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of art cited by patent owner during prosecution (IDS in reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art submitted in a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 1.555 (an IDS filed in a reexamination is construed as a prior art citation) may be used by the examiner and can cause the next Office action to be made final under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is not accompanied by a statement similar to 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the submitted art and make the next Office action final whether or not claims have been amended, provided that no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on new art not cited in the prior art citation. See MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Office actions in reexamination proceedings must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signatory requirement applies 'as with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice: limits on further prosecution and required conspicuous development of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: After entry of a final rejection that is not premature in a reexamination proceeding, the patent owner no longer has a right to unrestricted further prosecution; amendments and further consideration are governed by tight statutory/regulatory standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; amendments after appeal are governed by 37 CFR 41.33. Patent owners cannot refile under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d), and cannot request continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114. Both examiner and patent owner should identify and develop all issues prior to the final Office action, including presenting evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132. A patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to request withdrawal of a final rejection or entry of an amendment; the petition must be filed within the time period for filing a notice of appeal and does not toll the time for filing an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for entry of amendments after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection and prior to the appeal brief requires a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) if it touches the merits of the patent under reexamination; certain limited amendments may be entered without such a showing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that merely cancel claims, adopt examiner's suggestions, remove issues for appeal, or otherwise require only a cursory review by the examiner may be excepted. The first proposed amendment after final action will be given sufficient consideration to determine whether it places all claims in patentable condition or reduces/simplifies issues on appeal. If a proposed amendment is not entered in its entirety, the examiner will briefly explain reasons for not entering it (e.g., it presents a new issue requiring further search). The patent owner should be notified if parts of an amendment would be entered if submitted separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for handling defective or informal responses filed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bona fide response (even informal or unsigned) is filed after final rejection and before expiration of the permissible response period, specific procedures apply rather than issuing standard defect notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should not issue a PTOL-475 or PTO-2311 notification (the usual defect notices) after a final Office action. Instead, the examiner should issue an advisory Office action (e.g., form PTOL-467) with an explanation of the omission or defect. The practice of giving a time period to supply an omission (MPEP § 2266.01) does not apply after a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal eligibility and notice requirements in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the patent owner may appeal decisions in ex parte reexamination proceedings; third party requesters may not appeal or participate in the patent owner's appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice of appeal need not be signed (see 37 CFR 41.31(b)), but the fee required by 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) must accompany the notice. The period for filing the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally two months). The timely filing of a first response to a final rejection having a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the period for response an additional two months, provided the period does not exceed six months from the date of final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing defective notices of appeal and related forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When a notice of appeal is defective, the patent owner is notified and provided a period to cure the defects; different forms and cure periods apply depending on the type of reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In third-party requested reexaminations, Form PTOL-475 is used to notify and a cure period of one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) is provided. In patent-owner requested reexaminations or Director-ordered reexaminations, Form PTO-2311 is used and a two-month cure period is provided. An explanation of the defects must accompany the form. Failure to timely file a notice of appeal and/or the appeal fee will result in dismissal of the appeal (Form PTOL-468 may be used) and termination of reexamination prosecution, followed by issuance of a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and formatting for the appeal brief in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal briefs must comply with 37 CFR 41.37 and applicable MPEP instructions: include authorities and arguments, a summary of claimed subject matter with references to specification pages/lines and drawings, copies of the claims involved, and required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee as set in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) is required for the first filing of an appeal brief. Only one copy of the brief is required. The copy of the claims should be double spaced and start on a new page; claims on appeal in reexamination must include all underlining and bracketing required by 37 CFR 1.530(f) to reflect changes during prosecution. Any new claims added during reexamination should be completely underlined (departure from MPEP § 1205.02 for applications). The brief should indicate the art unit and reexamination control number. Briefs must be responsive to every ground of rejection; a reply brief, if filed, shall be entered, but amendments/affidavits/evidence remain subject to 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33. The Board expects briefs to fully state the appellant's position so no search of the record is required to determine that position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to seek Board review of a substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain Board review of an examiner's SNQ determination in ex parte reexamination ordered on or after June 25, 2010, the patent owner must first request reconsideration before the examiner and then include the SNQ issue and arguments in the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner must identify the communication in which reconsideration before the examiner was first requested (e.g., patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or response under 37 CFR 1.111). The Board's final decision may include a separate section reviewing the procedural SNQ issue and the merits of rejections. The patent owner may file a single request for rehearing under 37 CFR 11.52 for both SNQ and merits, resulting in a single final decision for judicial review (direct to the Federal Circuit under 35 U.S.C. 141). For ex parte reexaminations ordered prior to June 25, 2010, the Board historically reviewed SNQ issues presented in the appeal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of defective appeal briefs and the division of responsibilities between Board and examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Since May 25, 2010, the Board has sole responsibility for determining compliance of appeal briefs with 37 CFR 41.37 and will complete that determination before forwarding the brief to the examiner; examiners are no longer to hold briefs defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board determines a brief is non-compliant, the Board will notify appellant to file a corrected brief within the time set to avoid dismissal. Examiners should report serious defects that prevent drafting an examiner's answer to the Director of CRU, who will communicate with the Board if appropriate. Once the Board accepts a brief as compliant, it will not later be held defective by CRU or the examiner. Examiners are not required to determine whether fewer than all rejected claims are identified as appealed; the examiner should treat all pending rejected claims as being on appeal and maintain rejections unless overcome. A distinction is drawn between lack of any argument (which may justify summary sustainment of the rejection) and arguments that carry no conviction (which lead to a decision on the merits). Appellant must traverse every ground of rejection presented for review; oral argument will not remedy failure to traverse a ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer content, new grounds of rejection, and appellant options
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.39, the primary examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection from the Office action (as modified), unless expressly withdrawn; the examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection which must be designated as such and requires Director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner's answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground, appellant must within two months either: (1) reopen prosecution by requesting prosecution be reopened before the primary examiner by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits (§§ 1.130, 1.131 or 1.132) or other evidence relevant to the new ground (such a request will be entered and treated as a request to withdraw the appeal), or (2) maintain the appeal (other option text continues beyond the chunk). Any reopening will lead to reconsideration under 37 CFR 1.112.
